item.title: Statement – We Stand Together to Protect our Communities
item.description:
While the group “Crowborough Says No” claims to represent concerned local residents, the reality is that its platform has been built and supported alongside far-right political figures, extremist elements, and individuals with histories of criminality, violence, and racism.

The marchers flooding our streets are being bused in from all over the country—this is not genuine local concern. Local concern has been hijacked.

They are political agitators who have turned Crowborough into a political circus, disrupting our town and disturbing our peace.

item.title: Statement on Crowfest
item.description:
Stand Up To Racism is a very broad based organisation with support from faith and community organisations, trade unions and from across the political spectrum.

It promotes community unity and has been central to the response across Britain to far right violence & attempts to divide our communities. Most recently it led the response to the violent knife attacks on Muslim people in Edinburgh, bringing 5k people onto the streets. It was at the centre of mobilising half a million people in London on the Together Alliance unity demo on 28 March in opposition to growth of the far right.

item.title: Crowborough under siege by far right
item.description:
Agitators, mobs, and a community terrified to speak out.

CROWBOROUGH is at a breaking point. For four months, weekly protests have taken over the town, growing in power.

The protests have been attended by some of the most dangerous names in British politics.

THE FAR RIGHT AGITATORS

  • Nick Tenconi, who sparked outrage by calling for a “holy war” and branding asylum seekers as “rapists and drug addicts.”
  • Advance UK, who wore “ICE” baseball caps just days after the tragic murder of Renee Good.
  • Tommy Robinson’s stewards and associates like Liam Tuffs, along with extremist Mike Gott (aka Carl England).
  • Raise The Colours
  • AY Audits
  • Christin Konstantin
  • Reform
  • Instead of being turned away they were met with cheers from the crowd.

THE BETRAYAL

The community feels abandoned by those meant to protect them. Shockingly, Police and Crime Commissioner Katy Bourne has been seen alongside these protesters.

item.title: Open Letter: Demand for Accountable Community Safety
item.description:
To all community leaders, stakeholders, and statutory agencies:

Stand Up To Racism advocates for collective, systemic, and accountable community safety. We demand the unequivocal rejection of self-appointed vigilante groups in favour of professional, legal, and transparent safety initiatives.

The Risks of Unregulated Patrols

Unregulated patrols are not a legitimate form of protection; they fundamentally undermine community care and the rule of law:

  • Targeting the Vulnerable: These groups often target asylum seekers and refugees, inciting fear and hostility against Black and Asian communities. They threaten social solidarity and provide cover for racist violence.
  • Undermining Justice: Actions such as “private entrapment” or improper evidence collection compromise criminal investigations. Inadmissible evidence leads to collapsed prosecutions and erodes the justice system.
  • Lack of Accountability: These groups bypass mandatory vetting and oversight. Misusing limited “citizen’s arrest” powers (Section 24A, PACE 1984) creates unmanaged risks and potential legal charges for the actors involved, such as false imprisonment.
